triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was conditioned on the witness's exemplar line identity `entry_is_line_b` rather than Section 232 aluminum membership, so the 40% Brazil surcharge was added to aluminum entries the cited 9903.01.77 exception exempts.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 0: 20 changed lines, exactly two Brazil-gate hunks plus the steel proof re-grounding, nothing else. Diff read in full; provision resolution and follow-up-commit notes from index 0 apply verbatim.
triage.verifier_justification: The ch03 diff changes encoded meaning in exactly the way described: in both `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, the Brazil IEEPA carve-out flips from the witness's exemplar-line flag `entry_is_line_b` to the membership predicate `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, while the rule's own (unchanged) exception proof atom cites "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02." I verified against the pinned corpus that 9903.01.77 is the Brazil +40% IEEPA heading and 9903.85.02 is the §232 aluminum heading (note 19(g) aluminum products), so the source criterion is aluminum membership, not a single line; `entry_is_line_b` is the witness's aluminum exemplar HTS 7601.10.30.00 (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` has `formula: entry_is_line_b`), a fixture identifier with no basis in the cited text, and the fix re-grounds it — the textbook untraceable_branch, not merely a scope widening, since the clause was already encoded and only its grounding was wrong. The rest of the diff (steel `source:` string and 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02 proof atoms, formula still '0.50') is provenance-only and mechanical, so the fidelity finding rests solely on the gate lines, which is where the reader anchored it.

triage.verifier_notes: Refutations tried and rejected: (1) "mechanical" fails — the steel half of the diff is citation/excerpt-only, but two formula gates changed; (2) "not_a_defect / new scope never claimed" fails — the parent module already declares chapter-scale coverage and says "Membership-semantic ... section-232 aluminum/steel ... are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation", and `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` already existed as an input in the parent (used by the §232 aluminum component at pre-file lines 2744/2751), so the Brazil gate was a straggler inconsistent with both the module's own prose and its cited exception; (3) "tolerated placeholder" (cf. the deliberately retained beer/§338 `entry_is_line_d`, kept only "because no membership module exists") fails for the same reason — the aluminum membership input did exist. Residual doubt driving confidence below 0.9: this is an in-branch repair of the immediately preceding commit a9562cfd on PR #1300 rather than a fix to long-lived shipped content, and the commit subject ("b1.6: certify generalized component gates") never names the Brazil gate; the PR body explicitly calls only the §122 exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed". Also worth flagging for the reviewer: chapter 3 is fish/crustaceans, so no real ch03 line is §232 aluminum — the runtime bite of this identical generated edit lives in metal chapters (ch76 etc.), and all 100 generated chapter modules carry the same two lines, so this commit will present as ~100 near-identical candidates. Competing kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out reached the wrong population); I rejected it because the entity (CustomsEntry) is unchanged and the rubric's untraceable_branch explicitly covers a condition "re-grounded" off a basis absent from the source.
